meta.title: "You don't understand anything" — why your child loses arguments even when they're right | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to tell the difference between a personal attack and an argument, and not lose their position when they're the target. Game-based course for children aged 8–12.

hero.headline: "You don't understand anything!" — and your child has already gone quiet?
hero.subheadline: Instead of an argument — a personal attack. The child might be right, but gets thrown off topic. And loses the conversation without even knowing why.

media.alt: A child being thrown off topic instead of receiving a real answer

pain.title: "You're too young" — that's not an answer, it's a hit
pain.body:
"You don't understand anything", "you're too young", "there's no point talking to you". At school, at home, among friends. The child might have a perfectly valid point — but after words like that, they either go quiet or start doubting themselves. And the conversation is lost.

This isn't a weak position or a lack of confidence. It's a natural reaction to being hit: when the attack is aimed at you rather than your idea, it's hard to stay on topic. Instead of engaging with what was said, the conversation shifts from "what you said" to "who you are". The child ends up defending themselves instead of their point.

The result — they lose the conversation even when they were right. "Maybe I really don't understand", "better say nothing" — and a valid point goes unspoken.

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 8–12 year olds. At this age, children are most receptive to new thinking patterns and haven't yet formed rigid biases.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
